page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What the symbols mean
lines: K = calyx, C = corolla, A = androecium, G =
A bracket round a number means those parts are
fused. A line under G means the ovary is
steps.why: A floral formula is only read correctly if each symbol is read correctly, and the symbol key is easy marks.
common_mistakes: Writing K for corolla and C for calyx. K is calyx (from the German Kelch).
Leaving the brackets off K and C. Solanum sepals and petals are fused.
steps.memory_tip: Read the formula outside in: bract, symmetry, sex, then K, C, A, G in whorl order.
steps.margin_note: A short key of the symbols is worth one line each. Do not skip it.

steps.label: The formula

lines.text: Ebr Ebrl ⊕ ⚥ K(5) C(5) A5 G(2)

lines: Underline the G — that shows the ovary is
Five fused sepals, five fused petals, five free
steps.why: Each part of the formula is a fact about the flower, so writing the formula is writing the whole floral description in short form.
common_mistakes: Writing A(5). The stamens are epipetalous but they are free from one another, so A5 has no bracket.
Forgetting the line under G, which turns a superior ovary into an unmarked one.
steps.memory_tip: Solanum: five, five, five, two. K(5) C(5) A5 G(2), and only the G is underlined.
steps.margin_note: Write the formula on its own line and underline the G by hand.

insider_note: Most marks are lost on the brackets, not on the numbers. A5 is free, K(5) and C(5) are fused, G(2) is fused and underlined.
